![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14198442/assets/5e8383b56998815d4c981e72c946fdbf8de77ece15e52ca2ed5c7371c8f2c8af.png)

Find ${lim}_{x\to 3}{(\frac{4f(x)-12}{{x}^{2}-2x+2})}^{2}$ for the function $f(x)$ plotted above.
question.worked_solution:
Using the power and quotient rules, we can rewrite the given limit as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 3}{(\frac{4f(x)-12}{{x}^{2}-2x+2})}^{2} & ={(\frac{{lim}_{x\to 3}(4f(x)-12)}{{lim}_{x\to 3}({x}^{2}-2x+2)})}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

The above is true provided that  ${lim}_{x\to 3}f(x)$ exists.

We find from the graph that ${lim}_{x\to 3}f(x)=4.$ We calculate the limits of the numerator and denominator, separately.

$$
{lim}_{x\to 3}(4f(x)-12)=4(4)-12=4
$$

and

$$
{lim}_{x\to 3}({x}^{2}-2x+2)={3}^{2}-2(3)+2=5
$$

So we have
 

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to 3}{(\frac{4f(x)-12}{{x}^{2}-2x+2})}^{2} & ={(\frac{{lim}_{x\to 3}(4f(x)-12)}{{lim}_{x\to 3}({x}^{2}-2x+2)})}^{2} \\  & ={(\frac{4}{5})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{16}{25}\,.\end{aligned}
$$
